questions.question_english: Under the CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021 for Family Pension, in the case of twin children born to a deceased government servant, how is the family pension disbursed?
options_english: It is payable to both children in equal shares.
Only the elder twin receives the entire family pension.
It is paid to the surviving parent in trust, irrespective of the twins' ages.
The total family pension amount is doubled.
questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 50(7)(c) of the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 2021:
1. **Equal Shares for Twins:** Where family pension is payable to twin children of a deceased government servant, it shall be paid to both such children in **equal shares** (50% of the total family pension each).
2. **Subsequent Eligibility & Reversion:** When one of the twins ceases to be eligible for family pension (e.g., attains 25 years of age, marries, or begins earning a monthly livelihood exceeding the minimum family pension plus Dearness Relief), their 50% share does not lapse. Instead, the surviving eligible twin child becomes entitled to draw the entire 100% of the family pension.
3. **Exception to Seniority Rule:** Normally, under family pension rules, children receive pension strictly by seniority of age (eldest child first until disqualification). However, twins are deemed born simultaneously, creating an explicit statutory exception that mandates concurrent equal sharing.

2. **एक बच्चे की पात्रता समाप्त होने पर:** जब जुड़वां बच्चों में से किसी एक बच्चे की पात्रता समाप्त हो जाती है (जैसे 25 वर्ष की आयु पूरी कर लेना, विवाह होना, अथवा न्यूनतम पारिवारिक पेंशन + DR से अधिक स्वतंत्र आजीविका अर्जित करना), तो उसका हिस्सा समाप्त नहीं होता। इसके स्थान पर दूसरा पात्र बच्चा पूरी पारिवारिक पेंशन (100%) प्राप्त करने का हकदार बन जाता है।
3. **वरिष्ठता नियम का अपवाद:** सामान्यतः संतानों के मामले में पारिवारिक पेंशन सबसे बड़े बच्चे को दी जाती है, किंतु जुड़वां बच्चों को एक साथ जन्म लेने वाला माना जाता है, अतः नियमों में उन्हें एक साथ समान हिस्सेदारी का विशेष अधिकार दिया गया है।

questions.question_english: An employee was on unauthorized absence for four months, which the competent authority subsequently declared and treated as ‘dies non’. What is the effect of ‘dies non’ on the employee’s pension and past service?
options_english: The period is fully counted as qualifying service for pension, although pay and allowances are completely withheld
The period does not count as qualifying service, but it does NOT cause a break in service that forfeits past service
The period does not count as qualifying service and permanently breaks continuity of service, requiring presidential condonation
The employee is deemed to have automatically resigned and is stripped of all pensionary entitlements
questions.explanation_english: Under civil service regulations and Rule 27/28 of the CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021, when an unauthorized absence, strike, or non-duty spell is treated as 'dies non' (literally a day that does not count for anything), the specific period does not qualify for pay, allowances, leave accrual, increments, or pension calculation. Crucially, treating a period as 'dies non' does NOT constitute a 'break in service' (interruption) that entails forfeiture of past service. The service rendered by the employee prior to the 'dies non' period remains fully intact and protected for the determination of qualifying service for pension. In contrast, an un-condoned break in service under Rule 27 forfeits all past service. Therefore, 'dies non' merely acts as a gap excluded from qualifying service without wiping out previous service.
questions.explanation_hindi: सिविल सेवा नियमों और सीसीएस (पेंशन) नियम, 2021 के प्रावधानों के अंतर्गत, जब किसी अनधिकृत अनुपस्थिति या गैर-ड्यूटी की अवधि को सक्षम प्राधिकारी द्वारा 'डाइज नॉन' (dies non - अ-दिवस) घोषित किया जाता है, तो उस विशिष्ट अवधि के लिए कोई वेतन, भत्ता, अवकाश या वेतन वृद्धि देय नहीं होती और न ही वह अवधि पेंशन हेतु अर्हक सेवा में गिनी जाती है। सबसे महत्वपूर्ण बात यह है कि 'डाइज नॉन' को सेवा में ऐसा 'व्यवधान' (break in service) नहीं माना जाता जो कर्मचारी की पूर्व में की गई अर्हक सेवा को जब्त (forfeit) कर दे। कर्मचारी द्वारा उस अवधि से पूर्व की गई संपूर्ण सेवा सुरक्षित रहती है और पेंशन निर्धारण के लिए अर्हक सेवा में गिनी जाती है। अतः 'डाइज नॉन' का प्रभाव केवल इतना है कि वह 4 महीने की अवधि अर्हक सेवा से बाहर हो जाती है, किंतु पिछली सेवा नष्ट नहीं होती।

However, declaring a period as ‘dies non’ does not constitute a break in service that forfeits past service rendered prior to that period.

questions.question_english: Under family pension rules of the Central Civil Services, what is the eligibility condition for an unmarried, widowed, or divorced daughter of a deceased government servant to receive family pension beyond the age of 25 years?
options_english: She is strictly eligible to receive family pension only until she attains the age of 25 years, regardless of marital status or income level.
She is eligible for life if her monthly income is below minimum family pension plus DR, until she marries or remarries.
She is eligible to receive family pension only if there is no surviving son in the family capable of earning a livelihood.
She is eligible for a fixed maximum period of 10 years following the death of both parents, provided she remains unmarried.
questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 50(8) and Rule 50(9) of the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 2021, an unmarried, widowed, or divorced daughter is eligible for the grant of family pension even beyond the age of 25 years, and for life, subject to two statutory conditions: (i) until she gets married or remarried, and (ii) until she starts earning her own livelihood. The livelihood/dependency criterion established by the Government specifies that her monthly income from all sources must not exceed the minimum family pension (₹9,000/- per month) plus Dearness Relief admissible thereon. Unmarried, widowed, or divorced daughters are considered for family pension in the order of their birth dates, after all eligible sons under 25 years have ceased to be eligible (or concurrently with disabled children as per priority rules). The Head of Office (HOO) must require an annual income and non-marriage certificate to ensure continuous lawful disbursement.
questions.explanation_hindi: केंद्रीय सिविल सेवा (पेंशन) नियम, 2021 के नियम 50(8) और नियम 50(9) के अनुसार, किसी मृत सरकारी सेवक की अविवाहित, विधवा या तलाकशुदा पुत्री 25 वर्ष की आयु के बाद भी जीवन भर पारिवारिक पेंशन पाने की पात्र है, जब तक कि वह विवाह या पुनर्विवाह नहीं कर लेती अथवा स्वयं की आजीविका अर्जित करना प्रारंभ नहीं कर देती। आजीविका की निर्भरता शर्त यह है कि सभी स्रोतों से उसकी कुल मासिक आय न्यूनतम पारिवारिक पेंशन (₹9,000 प्रतिमाह) तथा उस पर अनुमेय महंगाई राहत (DR) से कम होनी चाहिए। 25 वर्ष से कम आयु के सभी पुत्रों की पात्रता समाप्त होने के बाद पुत्रियों को उनकी जन्म तिथि की वरिष्ठता के क्रम में पेंशन दी जाती है। कार्यालय प्रमुख (HOO) और बैंक को यह सुनिश्चित करना होता है कि पेंशनभोगी पुत्री प्रतिवर्ष निर्धारित गैर-विवाह एवं आय प्रमाण पत्र प्रस्तुत करे।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) She is eligible for life if her monthly income is below minimum family pension plus DR, until she marries.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: An unmarried, widowed, or divorced daughter of a deceased government servant is eligible for family pension until she marries or remarries, or until she begins earning a monthly income exceeding the statutory minimum family pension plus dearness relief. There is no strict upper age cap of twenty-five years for daughters.

questions.explanation_english: Under both the CCS (Pension) Rules, 1972 and 2021, the substantive principles governing qualifying service remain identical: service qualifies from the date of taking charge of a post, a minimum of 10 years of qualifying service is required for pension entitlement, and since the 6th CPC (delinked from 33 years), full pension is admissible after 20 half-yearly periods (10 years) of qualifying service. The major change introduced in the CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021 is administrative and procedural: Chapter VII of the 2021 rules mandates end-to-end digital verification of service through the electronic 'Bhavishya' platform, establishes strict statutory timelines for Head of Office (HoO) verification, and simplifies verification when service records are missing or partially incomplete.
questions.explanation_hindi: सीसीएस (पेंशन) नियम, 1972 और 2021 दोनों के अंतर्गत अर्हक सेवा (Qualifying Service) की मूल गणना संबंधी सिद्धांत समान बने हुए हैं। 10 वर्ष की न्यूनतम अर्हक सेवा पर पेंशन पात्रता प्राप्त होती है तथा पूर्ण पेंशन के लिए 33 वर्ष की पूर्व अनिवार्यता को समाप्त रखा गया है। 2021 के नियमों में प्रमुख सुधार प्रक्रियात्मक और प्रशासनिक है: इसमें 'भविष्य' (Bhavishya) ऑनलाइन पोर्टल के माध्यम से सेवा के डिजिटल सत्यापन को अनिवार्य किया गया है, कार्यालय प्रमुख (Head of Office) द्वारा 18 वर्ष की सेवा या सेवानिवृत्ति से 5 वर्ष पूर्व अर्हक सेवा के सत्यापन और कर्मचारी को प्रमाण पत्र जारी करने की समय-सीमा को कड़ाई से लागू किया गया है।

questions.question_english: Under the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 2021, which of the following periods does NOT count as qualifying service for the calculation of pension?
options_english: Continuous duty period rendered substantively in a regular government post
Extraordinary Leave (EOL) taken without a medical certificate, unless specifically authorized to count
Authorized period of joining time granted to an employee on transfer in public interest
Period of deputation on foreign service for which pension contributions have been duly paid
questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 21 of the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 2021 (Counting of periods spent on leave), all leave during service for which leave salary is payable and all extraordinary leave (EOL) granted on medical certificate count as qualifying service. However, Extraordinary Leave (EOL) granted without a medical certificate does NOT count as qualifying service, unless the appointing authority, at the time of granting such leave or subsequently, specifically sanctions that the period shall count as qualifying service on the grounds that such leave was taken on account of illness, inability to join duty due to civil commotion, or for prosecuting scientific and technical studies in public interest. In contrast, continuous duty rendered substantively (Rule 14), authorized joining time availed on transfer under CCS (Joining Time) Rules (Rule 23), and foreign service deputation periods where pension contributions are regularly remitted to the Government (Rule 24) fully count toward qualifying service.

questions.question_english: Which of the following is considered ‘Emoluments’ for calculating Family Pension under the CCS (Pension) Rules?

Basic Pay plus Dearness Allowance drawn on the date of death
Only the minimum pay of the pay band

questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 31 and Rule 50 of the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 2021 (corresponding to Rule 33 and Rule 54 of the 1972 Rules), the definition of 'Emoluments' differs between normal superannuation pension and family pension:

1. Superannuation/Retiring Pension: The pension is determined as 50% of either the 'Emoluments' (basic pay drawn on the date of retirement) OR 50% of the 'Average Emoluments' (average basic pay drawn during the last 10 months of service), whichever is more advantageous to the retiring official.
2. Family Pension: In sharp contrast, Family Pension does NOT use the 10-month average calculation. For Family Pension, 'Emoluments' strictly means the basic pay in the designated level of the Pay Matrix drawn by the government servant on the date of death (if death occurs while in service) or on the date of retirement (if death occurs after retirement).
3. Allowance Exclusion: Allowances such as Dearness Allowance (DA), House Rent Allowance (HRA), Transport Allowance (TA), or Non-Practicing Allowance (except where specifically counted as pay) do not form part of emoluments for family pension computation.

1. सामान्य सेवानिवृत्ति पेंशन: इसकी गणना सेवानिवृत्ति के समय आहरित अंतिम मूल वेतन (Emoluments) के 50% अथवा अंतिम 10 महीनों के औसत मूल वेतन (Average Emoluments) के 50%, जो भी कर्मचारी के लिए अधिक लाभकारी हो, के आधार पर की जाती है।
2. पारिवारिक पेंशन: पारिवारिक पेंशन के निर्धारण में 10 महीने के औसत वेतन की व्यवस्था लागू नहीं होती। पारिवारिक पेंशन के उद्देश्य से 'परिलब्धियों' का सीधा और स्पष्ट अर्थ कर्मचारी द्वारा सेवाकाल में मृत्यु की तिथि पर अथवा सेवानिवृत्ति की तिथि पर आहरित वास्तविक मूल वेतन (Basic Pay) है।

key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) Basic Pay drawn on the date of death or retirement

questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 50(9)(d) and (e) of the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 2021 (corresponding to Rule 54(6) of the 1972 Rules), if a son or daughter of a government servant is suffering from any mental disorder or physical disability which renders them unable to earn a living even after attaining the age of 25 years, the family pension is sanctioned to such disabled child for life. questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 45(1)(a) of the CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021 (corresponding to Rule 50(1)(a) of the 1972 Rules), Retirement Gratuity is admissible to a government servant who has completed a minimum of 5 years of qualifying service and has become eligible for service gratuity or pension on retirement. questions.question_english: Under the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 2021, what is the statutory formula for calculating Retirement Gratuity for a government servant retiring on superannuation?

One-half (1/2) of monthly emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service.

questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 45(1)(a) of the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 2021 (corresponding to Rule 50(1)(a) of the 1972 Rules), a government servant who has completed a minimum of five years' qualifying service and has become eligible for service gratuity or pension is granted Retirement Gratuity upon retirement. The formula prescribed is: Retirement Gratuity = [Emoluments / 4] × [Number of completed six-monthly periods of qualifying service]. This is mathematically equivalent to half a month's pay for each completed year of qualifying service. The maximum amount of retirement gratuity payable is subject to a ceiling of 16½ times the monthly emoluments, and it cannot exceed the statutory monetary cap (₹20 Lakhs, enhanced to ₹25 Lakhs when Dearness Allowance crosses 50%). Emoluments for this purpose consist of Basic Pay plus Dearness Allowance on the date of cessation of service. The Head of Office (HOO) must compute this via Form 7 / Bhavishya and submit it to the Pay and Accounts Office (PAO) for authorization.

questions.question_english: A school Principal, acting as the Head of Office, is processing the retirement papers of a PGT against whom a vigilance inquiry/departmental proceeding is pending. As per the CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021, what must the Principal do regarding the payment of Retirement Gratuity?
options_english: Disburse the full gratuity amount immediately on the superannuation date to avoid penal interest.
Disburse 50% of the gratuity amount immediately and withhold the remaining balance pending inquiry.
Convert the entire gratuity amount into a temporary non-withdrawable NPS Tier II account.
Withhold the entire gratuity until final orders are issued in the departmental or judicial proceedings.
questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 62(1)(c) of the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 2021:
1. **Mandatory Gratuity Withholding:** No gratuity shall be paid to a retiring government servant against whom departmental or judicial proceedings are pending on the date of retirement, until the conclusion of the proceedings and the issuance of final orders by the competent authority.
2. **No Provisional Gratuity:** While up to 100% provisional pension is sanctioned by the HoD, the rules strictly prohibit payment of any provisional gratuity during the pendency of disciplinary or court cases.
3. **Administrative Rationale:** This withholding protects public interest and government revenue. Under Rule 8 of CCS (Pension) Rules, if the employee is ultimately found guilty of grave misconduct or negligence causing financial loss, recovery can be made from the withheld gratuity.
4. **Duties of Head of Office:** The Principal/HOO must ensure that the PAO is explicitly notified via the Bhavishya system to withhold the retirement gratuity, while processing sanction for provisional pension.
questions.explanation_hindi:
केंद्रीय सिविल सेवा (पेंशन) नियम, 2021 के नियम 62(1)(ग) के अनुसार:
1. **उपदान को अनिवार्य रूप से रोकना:** यदि सेवानिवृत्ति की तिथि पर किसी सरकारी कर्मचारी के विरुद्ध कोई विभागीय या न्यायिक कार्यवाही लंबित है, तो ऐसी कार्यवाही समाप्त होने और सक्षम प्राधिकारी द्वारा अंतिम आदेश जारी किए जाने तक सेवानिवृत्ति उपदान (Retirement Gratuity) का कोई भी भाग संवितरित नहीं किया जाएगा।
2. **अनंतिम उपदान का कोई प्रावधान नहीं:** यद्यपि अनंतिम पेंशन 100% तक स्वीकृत की जा सकती है, किंतु नियमों में अनंतिम उपदान (Provisional Gratuity) का कोई प्रावधान नहीं है; संपूर्ण उपदान को शत-प्रतिशत रोकना अनिवार्य है।
3. **प्रशासनिक औचित्य:** यह प्रावधान इसलिए है ताकि जांच में यदि कर्मचारी द्वारा सरकार को वित्तीय क्षति पहुंचाए जाने की पुष्टि होती है, तो नियम 8 के अंतर्गत रोकी गई उपदान राशि से उसकी वसूली की जा सके।
4. **प्रधानाचार्य (कार्यालय प्रमुख) का कर्तव्य:** प्रधानाचार्य को वेतन एवं लेखा कार्यालय (PAO) को स्पष्ट सूचित करना होगा कि सतर्कता जांच लंबित होने के कारण उपदान रोक लिया जाए तथा केवल अनंतिम पेंशन का प्राधिकार पत्र जारी किया जाए।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) Withhold entire gratuity until final orders in departmental or judicial proceedings.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: When departmental or judicial proceedings are pending against a retiring government servant, the Head of Office must withhold the payment of Retirement Gratuity until the final orders are passed by the competent authority. No provisional gratuity is disbursed during the pendency of vigilance inquiries or formal disciplinary cases.

questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 40 of the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 2021 (Compensation Pension on abolition of post):
1. If a Government servant is selected for discharge from service owing to the abolition of his permanent post, he shall, unless he is appointed to another post the conditions of which are deemed by the authority competent to discharge him to be at least equal to those of his own, have the option of taking Compensation Pension.
2. The government servant may either opt to receive a Compensation Pension calculated on the basis of qualifying service already rendered, or accept an alternative lower appointment or transfer if offered with pay protection.
Therefore, premature exit forced upon a government servant strictly on account of administrative retrenchment or post abolition entitles them to a Compensation Pension.

For a period of 7 years from the date of death, or up to the date the deceased would have reached age 67, whichever is less
For a period of 10 years from the date of death, without any age limit restriction of the deceased
For the entire lifetime of the eligible spouse
questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 50(2)(a) and Rule 50(3) of the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 2021 (which codified the DoP&PW notification amending the earlier 1972 rules), where a government servant dies while in service (death in harness), enhanced family pension equal to 50% of the last pay drawn (or twice the normal family pension, whichever is less) is payable to the family for a fixed continuous period of ten (10) years from the day following the date of death. Crucially, under the modern 2021 rules, the earlier restrictive clause ('or until the employee would have attained 65/67 years of age, whichever is less') has been completely omitted for death in service cases. Moreover, the earlier prerequisite of completing a minimum of 7 years of continuous service was also amended by the Government to ensure that even families of employees who die with less than 7 years of service receive enhanced family pension for 10 years. After the expiry of the 10-year period, the family pension reverts to the normal rate of 30% of pay.

key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) For a period of 10 years from the date of death, without any age limit restriction of the deceased

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: When a government servant dies while in service, enhanced family pension equal to fifty percent of last pay or double the normal rate is payable to the eligible family for a fixed period of ten years from the day following death, without restricting eligibility based on the age the deceased would have reached.

questions.question_english: Identify the correct statement regarding the definition and computation of 'Average Emoluments' under Rule 32 of the CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021 for an OPS beneficiary:
options_english: It represents the average of the Basic Pay drawn during the preceding 24 months of continuous active service.
It is determined as the average of the Basic Pay drawn during the final 10 months of qualifying service.
It includes the aggregate of Basic Pay, Dearness Allowance, and House Rent Allowance drawn during the last 10 months.
It is computed on the basis of the single highest pay drawn at any point during the employee's entire official career.
questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 32 of the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 2021 (corresponding to Rule 34 of the CCS (Pension) Rules, 1972), 'Average Emoluments' is a fundamental concept used to determine the quantum of retirement pension.

Statutory Definition and Rules:
1. 10 Months' Calculation Window: Average emoluments are calculated with reference to the basic pay drawn by a government servant during the last ten months of their qualifying service immediately preceding the date of retirement.
2. Definition of 'Emoluments': Under Rule 31 of CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021, 'emoluments' means the Basic Pay as defined in FR 9(21)(a)(i) drawn by the government servant in the prescribed Level in the Pay Matrix. It does NOT include Dearness Allowance (DA), House Rent Allowance (HRA), Transport Allowance, or any other special allowances.
3. Statutory Rule 44 (Quantum of Pension): A retiring government servant is entitled to a pension calculated at 50% of the last pay drawn (emoluments) OR 50% of average emoluments, whichever is more beneficial to the employee, subject to the minimum monthly pension of ₹9,000 and the maximum ceiling of ₹1,25,000.
4. Processing through Bhavishya Portal: In modern pension administration, the Head of Office verifies the service book and enters the last 10 months' basic pay into the Bhavishya system, which automatically computes the average emoluments and applies the more beneficial 50% rate.
questions.explanation_hindi:
केंद्रीय सिविल सेवा (पेंशन) नियम, 2021 के नियम 32 (पूर्ववर्ती सीसीएस (पेंशन) नियम, 1972 के नियम 34) के तहत सेवानिवृत्ति पेंशन की राशि निर्धारित करने के लिए 'औसत उपलब्धियां' (Average Emoluments) एक मुख्य आधार हैं।

सांविधिक परिभाषा एवं नियम:
1. 10 माह की गणना अवधि: औसत उपलब्धियों की गणना किसी सरकारी कर्मचारी द्वारा अपनी सेवानिवृत्ति की तिथि से ठीक पहले की सेवा के अंतिम दस महीनों के दौरान प्राप्त मूल वेतन के औसत के आधार पर की जाती है।
2. 'उपलब्धियों' (Emoluments) का अर्थ: सीसीएस (पेंशन) नियम, 2021 के नियम 31 के तहत 'उपलब्धियों' से तात्पर्य वेतन मैट्रिक्स के निर्धारित स्तर में FR 9(21)(a)(i) के तहत प्राप्त 'मूल वेतन' (Basic Pay) से है। इसमें महंगाई भत्ता (DA), मकान किराया भत्ता (HRA), या कोई अन्य विशेष भत्ता शामिल नहीं होता।
3. नियम 44 के तहत पेंशन निर्धारण: सेवानिवृत्त होने वाले कर्मचारी को अंतिम आहरित वेतन के 50% या अंतिम 10 माह की औसत उपलब्धियों के 50% में से जो भी कर्मचारी के लिए अधिक लाभकारी हो, के आधार पर पेंशन दी जाती है (न्यूनतम ₹9,000 तथा अधिकतम ₹1,25,000 प्रतिमाह)।
4. भविष्य (Bhavishya) पोर्टल पर प्रक्रिया: कार्यालयाध्यक्ष (HoO) द्वारा सेवा पुस्तिका के आधार पर अंतिम 10 महीनों के मूल वेतन का सत्यापन कर 'भविष्य' पोर्टल पर प्रविष्ट किया जाता है, जो स्वतः औसत उपलब्धियों की गणना करता है।

questions.explanation_english:
Under the standing operating guidelines issued by the Department of Pension & Pensioners' Welfare (DoPPW) for Pension Adalats:
1. Admissible Grievances: Pension Adalats strictly deal with individual operational, administrative, and procedural grievances arising from the non-implementation or misinterpretation of existing rules. This includes delays in PPO dispatch, miscalculation of qualifying service, non-payment of Dearness Relief (DR) arrears, delay in family pension authorization, or calculation errors in commutation.
2. Non-Admissible Matters: Pension Adalats have no statutory authority to hear matters involving:
   - Changes or amendments in statutory pension rules or policy decisions of the Government.
   - Demands for extending benefits contrary to settled government policy.
   - Matters that are sub-judice before Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT), High Courts, or the Supreme Court.
Therefore, petitions seeking to alter statutory pension rules or policy frameworks (Option A) are strictly excluded.

2. गैर-विचारणीय मामले: निम्नलिखित मामलों पर पेंशन अदालतों में विचार नहीं किया जा सकता:

अतः विकल्प A सही उत्तर है।

Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): The CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021 do not fundamentally alter or determine the regular retirement pension benefits of employees covered under the National Pension System (NPS).
Reason (R): Employees appointed on or after January 1, 2004 are governed by the separate statutory Central Civil Services (Implementation of NPS) Rules, 2021, rather than the defined-benefit provisions of the CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021.
In the context of the statements above, which of the following is correct?

questions.explanation_english: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, and Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A). The CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021 are framed under the proviso to Article 309 and clause (5) of Article 148 of the Constitution to regulate defined-benefit pensions for government servants appointed on or before December 31, 2003 (Old Pension Scheme). Central government employees recruited on or after January 1, 2004 are governed by a distinct statutory framework, namely the Central Civil Services (Implementation of National Pension System) Rules, 2021 (notified on March 30, 2021). Therefore, the regular retirement benefits of NPS subscribers are derived from their accumulated defined contribution pension wealth under PFRDA regulations and the NPS Rules, 2021, rather than the defined-benefit calculations of the CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021 (with the limited exception of invalidation/death benefits under Rule 10 of NPS Rules).
